thread:
Maya: FYI we're getting a customer escalation — sudden spike of 502/503s after the 09:00 canary rollout. High-level: hosted inference API errors and timeouts.
Sam: seeing it in graph too, 503 rate jumped from 0.2% -> 6% at 09:07 UTC. Affected routes: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.
Jorge: oncall traces show downstream gateway returning 502 due to upstream auth failures; several customers report billing errors as tokens rejected.
Maya: can someone post recent deploy diff? I think a config flag flip for kvcache prefetched routes went out in the canary.
deploy-bot: deploy started by jenkins-ci at 2026-03-17T09:01:23Z - canary=10%, flags: kvcache_prefetch=true, strict_auth_trim=true
Evelyn: oh — strict_auth_trim=true was intended for private infra only. It strips unknown auth headers which some clients rely on (X-Customer-Token). That could explain 401 -> 502 cascade.
Sam: I can repro locally against canary tag. curl against canary gateway returns 502. Quick repro:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer valid-rl-token" -H "X-Customer-Token: 12345" \
  "https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```
Response shows upstream error: `upstream read timeout` then 502. Logs show auth middleware rejecting X-Customer-Token as malformed and dropping, which triggers route to upstream auth service that times out.
Jorge: stack logs snippet: `auth-mw: trimmed header X-Customer-Token -> missing; calling auth-v2 at endpoint auth-internal:443; auth-internal: timeout 10s`
Maya: is the rollback blocked? I see staged rollout is at 10% and orchestrator says new canary shards still draining.
Sam: rollback attempt failed because some canary pods couldn't update due to configmap lock from feature-gate controller. Error: `configmap update conflict - resourceVersion mismatch`. Trying manual patch now.
Evelyn: if configmap patching stalls, we should force revert at the routing layer: change route weights back to stable (90/10 -> 100/0). I can patch router weight in 2 mins.
Jorge: do that + disable kvcache_prefetch at runtime for canary nodes. Also set strict_auth_trim=false cluster-wide.
Maya: assignment: Evelyn patch routing weights; Sam help with canary nodes runbook; Jorge verify auth-internal health and postmortem checklist. I'll notify SRE and CS.
Sam: Applied weight rollback: `kubectl patch configmap router-weights -p '{"data":{"canary": "0"}}'` -> router noticed, traffic now 100% stable. Monitoring: 503s dropping back to 0.4% over 6 minutes.
deploy-bot: deploy rollback executed by Evelyn at 2026-03-17T09:19:12Z - canary weight -> 0%
Jorge: restarted auth-internal; heap speculation: tight retry loop + auth-backend timeouts caused backlog -> upstream gateway returned 502. Post-restart, auth-internal healthy.
Evelyn: billing team updated affected customers via status page. Noting a subset got billed errors because X-Customer-Token validation thrown 401 into billing flow. We'll open billing hotfix ticket.
Maya: followups: 1) remove strict_auth_trim from default flag set, 2) add configmap write health check before rollout, 3) add pre-rollout smoke that hits /v1/generate with X-Customer-Token variants.
Sam: putting a temporary rollout block rule on feature-gate-controller until we have the configmap check implemented.
Jorge: logging improvement: include which header was trimmed and prior value hash (no PII) to help repro.
Maya: thanks team. I'll convert this thread into an incident doc and schedule a postmortem. If anyone has extra traces or customer repros drop them here. :memo:
